overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the committee released the executive session minutes about 10 days late but had been unable to vote earlier, and the minutes were publicly released before the complaint was filed.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to release December 2018 executive session minutes within the 30 days required by the AG's prior order in OML 2019-161.
allegations.key_passage: Although we acknowledge that the Committee did not release the executive session minutes to the public within 30 days of receipt of our prior order, but rather released the minutes within approximately 40 days, we decline to find a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the released minutes were not effectively public because the links sent to him did not lead him to the document, so the order was not complied with.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, we note that the Committee had publicly released the December 20, 2018, meeting minutes, including by sending links to the minutes directly to Mr. Mackin, before Mr. Mackin filed this Open Meeting Law complaint.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
